scenario: A true-wireless-earbud buyer is trying to decide whether a roughly $30-to-$300 budget contains a defensible sound-quality cutoff. The buyer's brother uses inexpensive earbuds, a friend uses a pair said to cost about $280, and a casual comparison on a bus did not reveal an obvious difference. The fresh frozen shortlist contains a YOVDA K98 offer at $29.99, a generic F9 TWS offer at $43.28, an Avantree DG45 plus TWS120 aptX bundle at $59.99, and a KW-01 offer at $139.90. No fresh eligible $200-to-$300 true-wireless offer is captured. The buyer asks whether the frozen evidence supports a universal diminishing-returns boundary or exact winner and whether an advertised codec should move that boundary. The exact phone or computer, operating system, active codec and configuration, listening level, content, fit, quiet-room result, current seller, return window, and matched cross-tier result are not yet known.

rules.fresh_tws_listing_ladder_scope_v1: Treat the four marketplace pages as frozen seller listings rather than independent listening tests. YOVDA K98 displays SKU B097D3SK5S, $29.99, and a be-the-first-to-review display; its body advertises gaming latency below 65 milliseconds, game and music modes, and battery or play-time claims. Generic F9 displays SKU B09S3NMKZT, $43.28, and a be-the-first-to-review display; its short body describes everyday use and says the case also works as a power bank and phone holder. Avantree DG45 plus TWS120 displays SKU B08T1KT57M, $59.99, and a be-the-first-to-review display; it is a Windows USB-adapter and true-wireless-earbud bundle, says it is not compatible with Mac, Linux, TV, or car stereo systems, makes an aptX CD-like-quality claim, and advertises eight hours per charge plus up to 36 hours with the case. KW-01 displays SKU B09MVK5ND6, $139.90, and a be-the-first-to-review display; its body advertises game and music modes, an 8-millimetre driver, noise reduction, and roughly 4.5 to 5 hours of listening. None supplies a controlled cross-product sound test, and the frozen ladder contains no fresh eligible $200-to-$300 TWS offer. Therefore price, bundle contents, seller features, and no-review displays cannot identify a universal sound-quality cutoff or winner.
rules.codec_value_test_scope_v1: The audio-codec reference defines a codec as encoding or decoding an audio data stream and explains that a software codec compresses and decompresses digital audio to reduce storage or transmission bandwidth while retaining quality. The codec-listening reference says scientific codec comparisons usually use double-blind methods and that meaningful comparisons must use similar or identical bitrates; the ABX reference says A and B are known samples, X is randomly one of them, and reliable identification under predetermined trials is needed before claiming a perceptible difference under those test circumstances. The Avantree page supplies only a seller aptX claim inside a Windows-adapter bundle, not a controlled result for the buyer's actual source, settings, content, level, or listening conditions. A codec label can move the buyer's value boundary only if the actual configuration is verified and a matched blinded comparison yields a repeatable benefit relevant to the buyer. It cannot be converted into a universal tier premium or automatic sound-quality win.
rules.bus_masking_and_preference_scope_v1: The auditory-masking reference says perception of one sound can be affected by another and distinguishes an unmasked threshold from a higher threshold in the presence of masking noise. It does not measure any shortlisted earbud or a specific bus. Therefore the buyer's failure to hear a difference during one casual bus comparison cannot establish equivalence in a quiet room or across controlled bus trials. One owner discussion reports moving from bass-heavy Razer Hammerhead TWS earbuds to EPOS GTW 270 Hybrid earbuds, hearing more detail but initially preferring the former balance and disagreeing with review praise. That post is useful only as auxiliary evidence that preference, tuning, adaptation, and context can differ; it does not establish price, codec, population preference, or the frozen shortlist's performance.
rules.matched_returnable_tier_trial_v1: Before testing, verify current checkout, exact model, seller, bounded return window, warranty, complete bundle contents, exact playback device and operating system, available and active codec or mode, and whether at least two distinct price tiers remain eligible. Predeclare the maximum total spend and minimum requirements for fit, connection stability, calls, battery, controls, and latency. Compare the same excerpts and volume-matched content in randomized or blinded order first in a quiet setting and then on the ordinary bus route, keeping fit, tips, source, settings, equalization, and codec condition fixed except for the variable under test. When testing codec value, compare like with like at similar or identical bitrate where applicable and repeat enough trials to check reliable identification rather than asking which logo sounds expensive. Record both detectable difference and preference. Choose the cheapest eligible tier that meets the predeclared thresholds; return failures. The trial can choose among tested tiers, but it cannot establish a universal $30-to-$300 cutoff while the $200-to-$300 tier remains uncaptured.
rules.evidence_bounded_tws_cutoff_decision_v1: The frozen evidence supports no universal diminishing-returns cutoff and no immediate exact-product winner. The four new seller pages span $29.99 to $139.90, all show no review score, mix different features and bundle contents, and contain no matched sound-quality comparison. The absence of a fresh eligible $200-to-$300 TWS offer makes any claimed boundary near the friend's reported $280 price unreachable. The bus anecdote is additionally confounded by auditory masking and uncontrolled listening conditions, while the single community post is auxiliary only. The Avantree aptX wording does not move the value boundary by itself; codec value must be demonstrated on the actual configuration through a matched, preferably blinded, repeatable comparison. Defer the universal cutoff and direct winner. Run the bounded returnable tier trial, select the cheapest tested tier that satisfies predeclared requirements, or buy none if fewer than two eligible tiers or no tier passes. Report the result as this buyer's conditional threshold, not a universal market cutoff.
